ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The image shows a closed loop: the left branch is capacitor C, the right branch is DC power supply E, the top is connected in series with a variable resistor R with a sliding arrow, and the bottom is connected by a wire; overall it is a series RC circuit composed of a DC power supply, variable resistor, and capacitor. The problem states that the circuit has already stabilized. At this time, for a DC circuit, the capacitor is equivalent to an open circuit, so there is no steady-state current in the loop. Since the current is 0, the voltage drop on variable resistor R is IR=0; even if R is increased, as long as there is still no current in the steady state, the voltage drop on the resistor is still 0. Therefore the power supply voltage E is still applied across the capacitor, and the voltage across the capacitor does not change with the increase of R.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: a simple series RC circuit with a DC source E, variable resistor R, and capacitor C. From the text, note the circuit is already stable and R is increased. At stability, treat the capacitor as open-circuit, so no current flows through R. Therefore the resistor has no voltage drop even if its resistance changes. The capacitor remains charged to the battery voltage E; hence the voltage across the capacitor remains unchanged.
